summary: Manual design assessment passed. The node now defines auxiliary IPC lanes as owner-local lifecycle resources, keeps `IPCBridge.spawn_lane()` as a low-level transport primitive, and requires suspend/unmount to stop dependent work before disconnect while resume recreates lanes lazily.
checks: Research explains why the page-browser execution lane and the existing lifecycle helpers place ownership above the bridge transport layer.
Decisions choose owner-local lifecycle scopes over IPCBridge-global state and define the suspend/unmount versus resume sequencing for lane-bound work.
Acceptance criteria require local ownership, lazy recreation, and local degradation instead of daemon-wide disconnect semantics.
Implementation notes identify the bridge, screen base, widget resource scope, screen-content host, and page browser as the proving-ground file scope.
